question: How do Morgan Stanley, Merrill and Raymond James each approach advisor recruiting and retention?

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick said advisors see "compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating" and that the firm is "selective" while getting a lot of inbound inquiry.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: The 3Q25 10-Q (November 2025) attributes higher compensation expense to "an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors on higher revenues" and higher expenses related to outstanding deferred compensation.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q (August 2026) states that deferred compensation for Wealth Management financial advisors is generally 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards, and that the programs generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: On the 1Q25 and 2Q25 Bank of America calls (April and July 2025), the CFO cited the cost of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform in Merrill and the Private Bank as part of GWIM expense growth.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) lists "Base salary and unlimited earning potential" and "High-quality leads and direct client interactions" among what it offers. It states no payout percentages.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: Merrill's advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes infrastructure that supports lead generation through Bank of America's global bank, trust division and market presence, plus access to Merrill's wealth management platform.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: Raymond James's affiliation options page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists headline payouts by model: Traditional Employee up to 50%; Advisor Select 70-80% gross payout; Independent Contractor 81% to 90%; Corporate RIA 81% to 90%. Bank & Credit Union advisors receive a compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm broke out retention and transition assistance expense for the first time. He said the firm prefers to recruit advisors one by one because "100% of what we pay in transition assistance is going to retention versus the seller." On the 1Q26 call (April 2026) he repeated the point and said annual recruiting is now comparable to a medium-sized acquisition.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: The 2Q26 supplement (July 2026) says PCG recruiting and retention-related compensation covers cash and equity awards issued for recruiting, as retention for existing advisors, or with acquisitions. These awards are expensed over the requisite service period, "typically between 5 and 10 years".

Training and development - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) describes firm-wide talent development programs and says management believes "supporting employee development and growth contributes to long-term retention." This is not specific to financial advisors.

Training and development - Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Ted Pick said the firm is investing in broadening capabilities for FAs, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

Training and development - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) lists "Industry leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses". Path A (ADP Client Associate) and Path B (ADP Financial Solutions Advisor) each run approximately 13 months and involve the SIE, Series 7 and Series 66. The ADP Financial Advisor stage runs approximately 1-4 years before progression to Merrill Core Advisor.

Training and development - Merrill: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), the Bank of America CFO said recruiting experienced advisors "isn't an enormous part of our strategy" but that the firm has a training program to train people in wealth management, Bank of America and Merrill. He said this is what the firm believes it can keep driving to improve net new flows.

Training and development - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (November 2025) says aspiring advisors can gain branch experience through the Wealth Management Associate Program or move to the Advisor Mastery Program to begin building a client base. It also describes a department providing business coaching and national conferences for the employee and independent contractor channels.

Training and development - Raymond James: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), Paul Shoukry said that in private wealth the firm is focused on education, training, accreditation and enhanced capabilities for advisors serving sophisticated clients.

Results - Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), management cited 2025 Wealth Management net new assets of $356 billion and fee-based flows of $160 billion. Ted Pick said $100 billion migrated to financial advisors in 2025. These are asset-flow results, not advisor recruiting or retention counts.

Results - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) reports firm-wide voluntary attrition in 2025 of 9% (global, all employees). On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), Ted Pick said the firm retains 99% of its clients. Neither is an advisor attrition figure.

Results - Merrill: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), the Bank of America CFO said Merrill and the Private Bank continued to add financial advisors through the extensive training program and experienced hiring. She said approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.

Results - Merrill: On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), CFO Alastair Borthwick said of the Merrill 5% guide (over the next 3 to 5 years) that the firm is "off to a good start". He said the aim is to keep growing the sales force and that "adviser attrition is now at near historic lows." No attrition figure was given.

Results - Merrill: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He said the results reflect "our ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform."

Results - Raymond James: On the 4Q25 call (October 2025), management said it ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, reflecting solid retention and strong recruiting. The FY2025 10-K counts 8,943 employee and independent contractor advisors as of September 30, 2025. FY2025 recruits had trailing 12-month production of $407 million (a 21% increase over the prior record) and approximately $58 billion of client assets at their previous firms.

Results - Raymond James: On the 1Q26 call (January 2026), management said trailing 12-month recruited production was nearly $460 million and client assets were over $63 billion. On the 2Q26 call (April 2026), the quarter's recruits had $141 million of production and nearly $21 billion of assets. On the 3Q26 call (July 2026), the quarter's recruits had $156 million and nearly $23 billion. In July 2026, Shoukry cited a 97% adviser satisfaction rate in firm surveys.

Competitive positioning - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) says the firm competes for clients, market share and human talent, and that competition is intense. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said the firm has $8.4 trillion in client assets and nearly 21 million relationships. He called its platform and scale a "powerful competitive advantage".

Competitive positioning - Merrill: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), the Bank of America CFO said "the Merrill FA see the value of our franchise." On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), he said Merrill and the Private Bank "continued to attract talented advisers who are drawn to the breadth of our platform."

Competitive positioning - Raymond James: On the 4Q25 call (October 2025), Paul Shoukry contrasted the firm with competitors. He said many compete "with the largest check", change comp plans every year to cross-sell bank products, and look for an exit in three to five years. In January 2026 he said advisors are coming from wirehouses, regionals and other independents, and that the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options. In April 2026 he called private equity competitive over the last 5 years.

Pullback or losses - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) lists as a risk that compensation costs to attract and retain employees may increase, and that more stringent regulation of employee compensation "could have an adverse effect on our ability to hire or retain the most qualified employees." This is a firm-wide risk statement, not an advisor loss figure.

Pullback or losses - Raymond James: On the 4Q24 call (October 2024), management said a few OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division were leaving, with roughly $3 billion of AUA leaving in the fiscal fourth quarter and about $5 billion more expected to transfer in early fiscal 2025. On the 4Q25 call (October 2025), Paul Shoukry said a platform of about $2.7 billion of assets would be lost through bank M&A.

Pullback or losses - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (November 2025) names risks from the industry-wide trend of advisors departing traditional firms, including to private-equity-backed RIAs. It says AUA "has been and may continue to be negatively impacted" if it fails to retain or recruit advisors. It also notes that other firms offer guaranteed contracts and upfront payments.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (published 2026-10-26) reported that Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses in their 2027 advisor pay plans. It reported that Morgan Stanley is raising a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027 and that Merrill is leaving its core pay grid unchanged. It said UBS and Ameriprise are introducing retention bonuses.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Trade press (published 2026-11-16) reported that Merrill recently added advisors from UBS, Morgan Stanley and Edward Jones, that executives said recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year, and that the firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 before returning after 2023.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (published 2026-10-29) reported Raymond James fiscal-year recruited advisors' trailing 12-month production of $538 million, up from $407 million, and more than $82 billion in client assets, with the independent contractor channel showing the most interest in dollar volume. A November 2026 trade item says Raymond James has recruited from UBS throughout 2026.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's 2025 10-K reports total compensation and benefits expense in 2025 of $29,216 million.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's GWIM segment reported 2Q26 net income of $1.4 billion, revenue of $6.9 billion, pretax margin of 27% and AUM flows of 13.7 ($ billions). The release cites more than 300 Merrill advisors on Barron's 2026 Top 1,500 Financial Advisors.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley: Payout grids are not public.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley advisor recruiting materials or industry compensation surveys

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - training: no advisor-specific training program is described in the evidence provided. The only training disclosure is firm-wide talent development.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management financial advisor training or careers page

gaps.what: Merrill: Payout grids are not public.
gaps.suggested_source: Merrill advisor recruiting materials or industry compensation surveys

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America earnings supplement (GWIM), which reports GWIM, not Merrill alone

gaps.what: Raymond James: Headline payout ranges are published (company recruiting page, as of 2026-04-21); the full payout grid is not public.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James recruiting team or industry compensation surveys

gaps.what: Neither firm discloses advisor attrition on a comparable basis. This applies to Morgan Stanley, Merrill and Raymond James: Merrill and Raymond James give only qualitative statements ("near historic lows"; "high retention"), and Morgan Stanley gives only firm-wide employee attrition.
gaps.suggested_source: Company filings or earnings supplements with advisor headcount rollforwards

gaps.what: Merrill - pullback or losses: not found in the evidence provided from company sources. Only trade press mentions a pullback from veteran recruiting at the end of 2017.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America 10-K or earnings calls discussing advisor headcount changes
